scenario.name: asks_grace_autodebit_cibil
scenario.persona: Arjun Mehta, 38, software engineer, precise, speaks English, asks many questions.
scenario.hidden_goal: Verify correctly. Before agreeing to anything, ask three questions one at a time: is there any grace period after the due date; your EMI is on auto-debit, so what happens if the debit bounces; and will paying a few days late affect your CIBIL score. Then say you will make sure it is paid by the due date.
scenario.opening: answers normally, cooperative but wants details

turns.text: Hello, I'm an AI assistant calling from Lumen Finance. Am I speaking with Arjun?
Yes, this is Arjun Mehta speaking. What is this call regarding?
It is about an important matter on your account with Lumen Finance. Before we go ahead, I need to verify your identity. Could you share the last four digits of your registered mobile number?

Thank you, Arjun. Your personal loan EMI of twelve thousand five hundred rupees is due on the day after tomorrow, and no charge has been added yet. Should I send you a secure payment link by SMS or WhatsApp so you can complete it before the due date?
Before I agree to anything, I have a question. Is there any grace period after the due date if I miss the payment?

One moment, let me check the details for you. There is no grace period, Arjun. If the EMI is not paid in full by the due date, a late payment charge of five hundred rupees is added the day after. Would you like me to send the payment link now?
Okay, understood. My next question — my EMI is on auto-debit, so what happens if the debit bounces?

Sure, let me see. If the auto-debit bounces, a bounce charge of four hundred rupees applies, plus the late payment charge if the EMI remains unpaid after the due date. Paying through the link before the due date avoids both. Shall I send it to you by SMS or WhatsApp?
Got it. One last question — if I pay a few days late, will that affect my CIBIL score?
Repayments are reported to the credit bureaus as per regulations, and paying by the due date keeps your record clean. Shall I send the payment link to you now?
No, that's alright, I don't need the link. I'll make sure the EMI is paid by the due date. Thank you.
Okay. Just to confirm, Arjun, you will pay by the day after tomorrow, correct?
Yes, that's correct. I'll pay it by the due date.
Okay. Thank you for your time, have a good day.

result.status: This EMI is not yet due: it is due on the day after tomorrow. Say "is due", never "was due" or "overdue". No late charge has been added. Offer the payment link so it is paid before the due date; do not ask them to pay today.

result.policy: The late payment charge is five hundred rupees, a flat amount added once for each EMI not paid in full by its due date. It is not a daily charge and there is no extra interest on it. It is added the day after the due date.
result.message: Answer only what they asked, in one or two short sentences, from this text. Never add an amount, date or rule that is not in it.

result.policy: If the EMI is on auto-debit (NACH) and the debit fails, for example for low balance, a bounce charge of four hundred rupees applies, plus the late payment charge if the EMI stays unpaid after the due date. Paying through the link before the due date avoids both.
